spec.cue: Three kinds of colour sensor and a picture nearly as sharp as yours.

primate_trichromat.note: peaks near 430, 531 and 561 nanometres, as in a macaque

rows: A macaque has three kinds of colour sensor, most sensitive near 430, 531 and 561 nanometres. That is close to your own set, so the colours stay much as you know them.
Owl monkeys have only one kind of cone and lack colour vision. Male marmosets have two kinds. Howler monkeys have three. This view draws the three-cone case.

A rhesus monkey reached 26.3 cycles per degree, and a marmoset's cone mosaic could support close to 30. A person sees about 30, so the picture is only slightly softer. A mouse lemur manages about 4.9, which is far blurrier.
Most monkeys have a fovea, a small pit in the retina where cones are packed closely. Squirrel monkeys show it clearly. Owl monkeys have only a rudimentary one.
Cells in the visual cortex of macaques respond to the small differences between the two eyes' views. Diurnal primates use these differences to judge distance among branches.

One sharpness value stands for all primates, and the app picks it between two measurements. The colour matrix is the app's mapping of three measured peaks onto your screen. The drawing option for colour is also the app's.
